groups.text: It is currently 16 degrees and raining in Berlin-Tempelhof.
With the morning weather set, here is the news.

A judicial magistrate in Islamabad has granted the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency a three-day physical remand of journalist Bilal Ghauri. The case falls under the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act, specifically regarding allegations that Ghauri disseminated false information about the appointment of the head of the National Counter Terrorism Authority. While the agency claims the content was misleading and lacked a factual basis, Ghauri’s lawyer argues his client was arrested without prior notice. In separate technical news, developers are addressing build failures in PyTorch's unified manywheel jobs. A root cause analysis found that changing absolute paths for CMake commands caused XPU iterations to take roughly 64 minutes each, far exceeding the 420-minute timeout. To fix this, engineers are pinning one cmake/ninja instance at the front of the path to ensure stability across Python ABIs and allow Ninja to reuse previously built device objects.

Russian attacks have killed at least three people and wounded 38 others across Ukraine. This violence follows a visit to Kyiv by Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, envoys for U.S. President Donald Trump who traveled there for talks on ending the war. Overnight, Russian forces launched 92 attack drones, though the Ukrainian Air Force reports that 71 were intercepted or shot down. The casualties are spread across several regions. In southern Kherson Oblast, two people died and 14 others were wounded. A person was killed and six more injured in central-eastern Dnipropetrovsk Oblast. Additional injuries were reported by regional governors in northeastern Kharkiv, southeastern Zaporizhzhia, and eastern Donetsk Oblasts.

In Lebanon, overnight Israeli strikes in the south have killed at least ten people, including two children. This escalation coincides with a sharp drop in maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, which has hit its lowest level since May. Iran is responding to these regional tensions by warning against any foreign military deployment in the Persian Gulf or the Strait, specifically as South Korea considers contributing to security operations there. Meanwhile, in Singapore, Swire Shipping is consolidating its operations by folding its specialist project and heavy lift arm into the main brand this November. The company is acquiring four multipurpose heavylift vessels to strengthen its capacity for infrastructure and energy projects across Asia Pacific. In a different vein, US President Donald Trump has suggested renaming the state of New Mexico to "New America." Governor Michelle Lujan Grisham rejected the proposal, calling it a distraction from rising gasoline prices and the war in Iran.

The video game industry is facing a slow-motion crash as the blockbuster model reaches a breaking point. Epic CEO Tim Sweeney describes this as the worst disruption since the 1980s, though he notes it differs from the era when Atari collapsed due to poor distribution and mediocre games. Today, the sector sees stagnant console markets and widespread layoffs while players spend less and rotate between only one or two titles. In a different corner of hardware, developers are working to bring Linux to Mac computers using Apple Silicon. The Asahi project has now integrated official support for M3, M3 Pro, and M3 Max chips into its installer, though the Ultra version remains unsupported. Because Apple does not provide technical documentation for its closed architecture, these developers must rely on reverse engineering and firmware analysis to make a free operating system function on the hardware.

A federal court has sentenced David Alfonso Barrera Nunes to 57 months in prison for his role in a smuggling operation that left five people dead. Last November, Border Patrol agents attempted to intercept Barrera's vessel crossing north from Mexico toward Imperial Beach, but dense fog blocked their visibility. The boat eventually capsized in rough surf; while passengers drowned, Barrera ran inland and climbed over a rock into a backyard without attempting any rescues. He had agreed to pilot the boat in exchange for a reduced smuggling rate. In a different kind of crisis, community-based warnings saved roughly 900 students at Tribhuvan Trishuli Secondary School during floods in Nepal on August 26. Head teacher Rajendra Dawadi ordered the evacuation after receiving frantic phone calls, just ten minutes before debris buried the school. Despite these local successes, the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority reports 1,252 deaths across five districts.

Germany is facing a sharp political shift as the far-right AfD party secures a major electoral victory. This surge in support comes amid a structural economic crisis and friction over the country's fiscal policies. While the political climate tightens, Germany has reached a significant milestone in aerospace technology. The startup Isar Aerospace has become the first private company in Europe to achieve a successful orbital space launch. These two events highlight a stark contrast in the country's current state, where high-tech industrial achievement is occurring alongside deep internal political instability and economic strain.

Enterprises are struggling to identify and manage security risks as cloud adoption accelerates. This vulnerability is highlighted by a full-day virtual event on securing cloud assets in the age of AI, which focuses on tools for managing multi-cloud environments. The urgency follows a year where nearly every organization faced a critical security incident, yet most lacked the equipment to contain them. New threats are also emerging from agentic AI, which presents a new insider threat model for organizations. These systemic risks contrast with specific, targeted disruptions, such as a Wi-Fi hack that disrupted a Delta flight in August. To address these gaps, experts are emphasizing the need for comprehensive insight into cloud infrastructure to get ahead of attackers. This shift toward better visibility comes as companies attempt to reconcile rapid digital expansion with the reality of an increasingly sophisticated threat landscape.
After the headlines, back to the weather.
This afternoon will be cloudy with rain chances up to 48 percent and temperatures between 16 and 28 degrees.
And from the weather, a quick look at the calendar.
On your calendar today: Your personal calendar has the BLISS Reading Group at six forty-five in the evening, followed by Twerchhau at seven.
Mail worth checking: Info sent a reminder about the Linux Stammtisch this Wednesday at 7 PM.
And that's it for your personal morning broadcast.
[mature adult voice, intensely emotional, tender, radiant; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
[very very long pause before speaking; then mature adult voice, most emotional, strong, warm, radiant, deeply encouraging; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
